StockSathi
Restocking and credit for India's small-town kirana stores
Pre-seed deck | Raising INR 2 Cr | Hyderabad

Kirana owners restock the hard way
StockSathi 2
3 trips a week
Owners travel to the nearest
wholesale market, losing half
a day each time.
No credit
Banks do not lend against
stock. Informal suppliers
charge 3 to 4% a month.
No price view
Prices vary by distributor and
by day. Owners rarely know if
they overpay.
Based on 60 owner interviews in Karimnagar and Warangal, June to July 2026.

Why now
StockSathi 3
UPI everywhere
Almost every store takes UPI.
That gives a payment trail we
can use to judge credit.
Quick commerce
Quick-commerce apps are
pulling customers from small
stores. Owners now need
better prices and stock.
Phones and voice
Cheap smartphones and
local-language voice input let
owners order without typing.

Order, get delivered, pay later
StockSathi 4
1
Order
Owner picks items in a simple
vernacular app
2
Deliver
Next-morning delivery from
partner distributors
3
Pay later
7 to 14 days credit on repeat
orders

38

Market size: how we got there
StockSathi 6
TAM INR 17 lakh Cr 12M kirana stores x INR 1.2 L monthly purchases x 12
SAM INR 64,800 Cr ~450K stores in Tier 3 to 5 towns of Telangana and AP x INR
1.2 L x 12
SOM INR 518 Cr In 3 years: 2% of SAM stores (9,000) x 40% of their purchases
(INR 48K a month) x 12
Assumptions: INR 1.2 L monthly purchases per store from our 60 owner interviews. Store counts are our estimates.

We earn on every order, and on credit
StockSathi 8
Trade margin
About 4% margin from distributors on every
order delivered.
Credit fee
1.5% fee on credit orders. Pilot with 12 retailers,
funded from our own capital for now.
Credit is about a third of October GMV. NBFC partnership in discussion.

The team
StockSathi 10
Aarav Deshmukh, CEO
8 years in FMCG distribution and field

Pooja Nair, CTO
5 years as a software engineer at a payments
company. Built the ordering app and credit rules.
Both full-time since April 2026. Two field agents on the team.
